name: Storybloq/storybloq
summary: Keeps a coding agent's decisions, plans and handovers as plain files in your repository, so the next session starts where the last one stopped.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: First-class but narrow. Installation is a single npm command with a setup flag that connects all supported clients, and the product ships both a CLI and a local MCP server, so an agent reads and writes the project record over MCP with no hosted quota or network round trip. Context is reloaded with one slash command in Claude Code or one dollar command in Codex. Because the record is plain files under .story/, any agent with filesystem access can consume it directly even without MCP - but the supported, documented path covers only Claude Code and Codex.

hlido_opinion.headline: Keeps a coding agent's decisions, plans and handovers as plain files in your repository, so the next session starts where the last one stopped.
hlido_opinion.body: The problem Storybloq names is the one every team using coding agents hits around week three: the agent is fast until the context is gone, and then each new session re-derives what the last one already knew. Its answer is deliberately unglamorous. Stories, issues, lessons and handovers live in a .story/ directory beside the source, as plain files you open, edit, version and review in Git. The CLI and MCP server run locally, with - stated explicitly - no Storybloq cloud subscription, no hosted-MCP quota and no network round trip to read your own project record. That is the correct architecture for this problem and it is the main reason the product is credible: the thing of value stays in the repository, so the tool can be abandoned without losing the record. The handover structure is specific rather than hand-waved - what changed, why it changed, and what comes next, with open questions and blockers - and loading it back is a single command in Claude Code or Codex. Multi-repo federation addresses a real gap, letting work across web, API and mobile be seen as one picture while each repository keeps its own history. The most creditable line on the whole surface is a disclaimer: review evidence helps you inspect the work, it does not guarantee correct code, and tests, CI and release checks still matter. A tool selling agent oversight that volunteers the limits of its own oversight is making a claim we can actually trust. What holds the score down is evidence: no operating history, no demonstration, nothing captured on pricing or support, and only two named agent clients.

tier_rationale: STEADY (70) because the architecture matches the problem - the project record is plain files in the user's own repository, versioned in Git, with the CLI and MCP server local and no hosted dependency - the handover contract is specified concretely, multi-repo federation addresses a genuine gap, and the surface volunteers the limits of its own review evidence rather than overselling it. Not VITAL because no operating history or release cadence is visible, nothing on the captured surface demonstrates the product working, no clear primary action or access terms were present, the field notes are the vendor's own writing rather than third-party validation, and support is confined to two named agent clients, so anything else is unaddressed.
what_it_does_well: Keeps the valuable artifact - stories, issues, lessons and handovers - as plain files in the user's own repository, versioned in Git and editable by hand
Runs the CLI and MCP server locally and states plainly that there is no cloud subscription, no hosted-MCP quota and no network round trip to read your own project record
Specifies the handover contract concretely: what changed, why it changed, and what comes next including open questions and blockers
Reloads project context with a single command in Claude Code or Codex, so the recovery step is one action rather than a procedure
Addresses multi-repo work as a first-class case, keeping one picture of progress while each repository keeps its own history
Volunteers the limits of its own review evidence - that it aids inspection but does not guarantee correct code, and that tests, CI and release checks still matter
Recommends the next story based on blockers, unfinished work and what each story would unblock, rather than a flat backlog
Makes autonomous execution and independent review optional rather than the default
what_it_fails_at: No operating history, release cadence or maintenance commitment is visible
Nothing on the captured surface demonstrates the product in use - no recorded session, no example repository, no trace
No pricing, support terms or access model was captured beyond source-available with no account required
Only Claude Code and Codex are named as clients, leaving every other agent unaddressed
The field notes offered as depth are the vendor's own writing, not third-party validation
No clear single primary action was present on the captured surface
best_for: Teams whose coding-agent sessions keep re-deriving context that an earlier session already established
Operators who want the project record to survive the tool - plain files in Git rather than a vendor's database
Projects spanning several repositories that need coordinated progress without merging their histories
Anyone who needs a reviewable record of what an agent decided and why, for a human to inspect later
not_recommended_for: Teams using agents other than Claude Code or Codex, which are the only named clients
Organisations needing a hosted, managed service with support, since the design is deliberately local
Anyone expecting the review features to assure code correctness - the vendor itself says they do not
Single-session or throwaway work, where the overhead of a project record earns nothing
red_flags: No operating history or maintenance commitment for a tool asking to own the project's memory - the artifact survives in Git, but the workflow around it does not
The two supported clients are both vendor-controlled products, so the tool's usefulness tracks decisions made by Anthropic and OpenAI rather than by Storybloq

compared_to.verdict_diff: Claude Code is one of the two agents Storybloq harnesses, not an alternative to it - Storybloq adds the persistent project record, handovers and multi-repo coordination that Claude Code does not keep between sessions. Choose Claude Code alone for short tasks; add Storybloq when sessions must build on each other.

Letta provides persistent memory inside an agent runtime; Storybloq keeps the record as human-readable files in your repository, reviewable in Git. Choose Letta for memory an agent manages itself; choose Storybloq when a human needs to read, edit and version the same record.

evidence_urls.claim: A harness for Claude Code and Codex that coordinates agents, reviews their work and carries context between sessions
Stories, issues, lessons and handovers live as plain files in a .story/ directory beside the source, editable and versionable in Git
The CLI and MCP server run locally with no cloud subscription, hosted-MCP quota or network round trip to access the local project record
A handover records what changed, why it changed, and what comes next including open questions and blockers
The vendor states that review evidence aids inspection but does not guarantee correct code, and that tests, CI and release checks still matter
Installs via a single npm command; source-available with no Storybloq account required
